g1.correct: Covered in cardboard, paint and half-finished posters
accept: Covered in cardboard, paint and half-finished posters
g1.label: 1. What does Lena’s kitchen table look like on Thursday evening?
g1.why: The opening sentence says the kitchen table is covered in cardboard, paint and half-finished posters.

g2.label: 2. How many students had signed the pledge by Thursday morning?
g2.why: The text says that by that morning, more than two hundred students had signed the pledge.

g3.correct: Like a fire drill, so nobody will be punished
accept: Like a fire drill, so nobody will be punished
g3.label: 3. How have the teachers agreed to treat the walkout?
g3.why: Paragraph two says teachers agreed to treat it like a fire drill, with no punishment for taking part.

g4.correct: Because the council will be deciding on the new cycling budget next month
accept: Because the council will be deciding on the new cycling budget next month
g4.label: 4. Why does Lena say the timing of the action day matters?
g4.why: The text explains the timing matters because the council decides on the new cycling budget next month.

g5.label: 5. In "we will have collected hundreds more signatures", what tense is it?
g5.why: Will have + past participle looks back from a future point — the form is future perfect.

g6.label: 6. (Review) In "nobody will be punished", what voice is the sentence in?
g6.why: Review from 10g-scottish-history: the subject receives the action — will be + past participle is passive.

g1.label: 1. We’ve printed 300 flyers, and we ___ them to students.
g1.why: Going to expresses a plan or intention decided before speaking.

g2.label: 2. I honestly believe that my generation ___ change the world.
g2.why: Will is used for a prediction or personal opinion about the future.

g3.label: 3. The council meeting ___ at 7 pm.
g3.why: Present simple expresses fixed events in timetables and official schedules.

g4.label: 4. I ___ my grandparents on Saturday.
g4.why: Present continuous expresses a fixed personal arrangement for a future time.

g5.label: 5. Don’t worry about the posters — I ___ them tonight.
g5.why: Will expresses a spontaneous decision or offer made at the moment of speaking.

g6.label: 6. Scientists predict that global temperatures ___ by more than 1.5 degrees.
g6.why: Will is used for formal predictions, for example based on scientific evidence.

g7.label: 7. We ___ the head teacher tomorrow at ten.
g7.why: Present continuous marks a fixed arrangement — the head teacher is expecting them.

g8.label: 8. The coach to the demonstration ___ at 6.45 from platform two.
g8.why: Present simple is used for departures in timetables: the coach leaves at 6.45.

g1.label: 1. By the end of the month, our group ___ 1,000 signatures.
g1.why: By the end of the month looks back from a future point — use the future perfect.

g2.label: 2. This time tomorrow, we ___ banners in the courtyard.
g2.why: This time tomorrow marks an action in progress at a future moment — future continuous.

g3.label: 3. By 2050, sea levels ___ by another 20 centimetres.
g3.why: By 2050 signals completion before a future point — the future perfect is needed.

g4.label: 4. At eight tomorrow evening, I ___ my speech.
g4.why: An action in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous.

g5.label: 5. When the council votes, we ___ 2,000 signatures.
g5.why: By the time the council votes, the gathering is complete — future perfect.

g6.label: 6. At midday on Friday, students ___ in the streets.
g6.why: At midday on Friday marks an ongoing action at a future moment — future continuous.

g7.label: 7. In June, the new bike racks ___ by the caretaker.
g7.why: By the June visit the work is complete, and the racks receive the action — future perfect passive.

g8.label: 8. This time next year, I ___ my bike to school every day.
g8.why: This time next year marks an action in progress around a future moment — future continuous.
